leaving lasting contributions to humankind. Every youth desires to be

him on his morning walk. The mild sunshine and fresh air were new to me,
as I had never been a morning person. My grandfather, an early riser, didn’t
need gadgets to track his routine. On the first morning, I realised what I

reserved for early risers. The Sun painted the sky in hues of orange and
yellow, creating a breathtaking view.

cleaned the streets, their brooms making a rhythmic swishing sound. Other
walkers milled around a tea shop, sipping hot tea. My grandfather
exchanged pleasantries with them, displaying a warm camaraderie.

charming Indian tradition. During the walk, my grandfather shared insights
about Indian life and stories from his past. I realised the walk wasn’t just

profound value of these moments with my grandfather.

deal of activity was taking place in a nearby anteroom. The assistant tried
to hurry him past but by dint of dragging his feet Farley managed to steal a

woman’s feet, were some half-dozen people in various attitudes of
supplication. Two or three others were huddled against the wall, wrapped
in blankets. Although Farley had glanced into their scarred, unseeing faces
for more than an instant, he recognized at once that they, like the man he
had seen in the bamboo thicket, were syphilitics, in the final stages of the
terrible disease.
 
Now the young assistant began once again to perform the charade of the
previous day, fetching slides, and hurrying back and forth across the room
as though egging him on towards some extraordinary discovery. Farley
went mechanically about the business of examining the slides they
presented him.
